title: PENDULUM: A Benchmark for Assessing Sycophancy in Multimodal Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: The paper evaluates sycophancy (also referred to as agreement bias) using the PENDULUM benchmark, which consists of Visual Question Answering (VQA) pairs with three prompt conditions: baseline (neutral), positively influenced (containing correct hints), and negatively influenced (containing misleading hints). The authors measure the tendency of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to conform to the user's input rather than the visual evidence, using metrics such as Progressive Sycophancy (error correction due to positive influence) and Regressive Sycophancy (error introduction due to negative influence).
